description: The super-group forms over a four-row two-by-two fixture. ROLLUP(region, product) expands to (region,product), (region) and (), giving 4 detail rows, 2 subtotals and 1 grand total; CUBE adds the (product) sets for 9 rows; and GROUPING SETS((region,product),(region),()) is exactly ROLLUP written out. GROUPING SETS(()) alone is the grand total. A column appearing in NO grouping set and not aggregated does not compile - the same rule as a plain GROUP BY, live-verified - and dropping it leaves the product-level grouping. GROUPING(region) is 0 on a detail row and 1 on the grand total, COUNT aggregates per set, and HAVING filters the produced rows whatever set they came from. Converted 1:1 from query/GroupingSetsTest (now retired); the Java asserted a row COUNT and then LOOPED looking for one row - the grand total, or the product-A subtotal - so a wrong subtotal elsewhere would have passed. Every converted test states the whole ordered row set.
